To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acetylcholine (ACh) and 5-hydorxytryptamine(5-HT) stimulate calcium influx and contraction by different mechanisms in bovine coronary artery.
acetylcholine produces a sustained contraction and calcium influx, whereas 5-HT produces a more transient contraction and calcium influx.
acetylcholine-activated calcium channels in the bovine coronary artery are not blocked by diltiazem.

the mechanisms of agonist-induced calcium mobilization in bovine coronary artery smooth muscle.

5-HT and ACh operate different receptor-operated calcium channel systems in the coronary artery smooth muscle.

acetylcholine contracts the bovine coronary artery by activating two calcium channels, one that is sensitive to 1 microM of the organic calcium channel blocker diltiazem, and another that is insensitive to 1 micro M diltiazem but is sensitive to 0.1-0.2 microM of verapamil.

1) 5-HT and cholinergic agonists mobilize calcium in the same way in the bovine coronary artery, and 2) the calcium channels activated by 5-HT are different from those activated by acetylcholinergic agonists, and the channels activated by 1 agent are not necessarily activated by the other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are two populations of calcium channels in the smooth muscle cell membrane, one population being sensitive to acetylcholine or 5-HT, and another sensitive to depolarization.
acetylcholine stimulates calcium influx via a receptor-operated channel and a voltage-dependent calcium channel, whereas 5-HT stimulates calcium influx only via a receptor-operate channel.
there appear to be two populations of calcium channels, which may be receptor-operated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium channels activated by acetylcholinesterase are different than those activated by 5-HT.

the contraction of coronary artery smooth muscle is a complicated process involving a number of different receptors and ion channels, and the relative contributions of the different pathways to contraction may depend upon the species, vascular bed and experimental conditions.
the contractile responses of coronary arteries are mediated by two populations of receptor operated calcium channels, one of which is inhibited by diltiazem.
